summary: Iteration 13 — My Tax Return final-section corrections VERIFIED. The new tests/test_my_tax_return_final.py suite (18 tests: TestPaymentDeadline + TestApprovalAndSubmissionModel + TestFinalDocuments) passes 18/18 in ~18s under the locked -n 2 --dist loadscope harness — including the two adversarial cases the user asked for (a) stale stored '31 January 2026' on a 2025/26 case is overridden on read to '31 January 2027' (proves it is derived not stored) and (b) approve v2 with two calculations present yields approved_version==2 (proves the version is dynamic not hard-coded). Full backend regression (all 15 test files, ignoring test_zz_demo_portal_state which resets demo data): 336 passed / 2 skipped / 1 failed in 268s. The one failure is tests/test_iteration7_audit.py::TestAccountantRBAC::test_accountant_cannot_see_other_accountant_case which PASSES in isolation (verified) — same class of pre-existing xdist parallel-worker race the previous iteration flagged (previously it was TestStatsAndAdmin::test_notifications_and_mark_all_read; this run it surfaced a different one), NOT a regression from the My Tax Return changes and not related to any of the four corrections. FRONTEND E2E on the demo client /my-return: page renders without any real console error; shows 'Ready for HMRC submission', 'You've approved your return. Your accountant will now submit it to HMRC — nothing more is needed from you.', 'Payment deadline: 31 January 2027', empty-state 'Final documents will appear here once available.'; DOES NOT contain '31 January 2026', DOES NOT contain 'authorised submission team', DOES NOT leak any raw enum (READY_FOR_SUBMISSION / CLIENT_APPROVED / SELF_ASSESSMENT); final-docs-panel testid present; version label shows 'Your calculation (Version 2)' sourced from the dynamic approved_version (demo client has 2 calc versions and approved v2 — matches what the backend returns). Mobile at 390px re-verified: '31 January 2027' present, no '31 January 2026', no 'authorised submission team'. Adversarial probes on final documents (attempted from another disposable client): download URL returns 403/404 and the other client's list never contains the id. No hard-coded version or deadline was reachable via any endpoint I probed.

action_items: Non-blocking: consider stabilising the small handful of parallel-worker races (test_iteration7_audit::TestAccountantRBAC::test_accountant_cannot_see_other_accountant_case, test_taxsimba_phase1::TestStatsAndAdmin::test_notifications_and_mark_all_read) — both pass in isolation and only flake under -n 2 loadscope when other workers seed data concurrently.

External work still required (unchanged from iter12): real HMRC MTD/SA API integration, real transactional email provider, live Stripe keys, production DNS/ingress + real Cloudflare CORS validation. All four corrections requested here work correctly WITHOUT any of those since the model is 'accountant records the outcome manually'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_calculations correctly OVERRIDES payment_deadline on read using payment_deadline_label(case tax_year). This is the right design because it repairs historic rows that stored a stale literal — verified end-to-end by test_stale_stored_deadline_is_overridden_on_read.

get_case now derives approved_version from db.client_approvals (nullable int) and only exposes submission_date/submission_reference when a SUBMITTED submission_record exists — cleanly separating 'client approved' from 'accountant filed and recorded'. approved_version==None before approval, ==record.version after, and dynamically equals 2 when v2 is approved.

record-submission endpoint is correctly gated to ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN (client → 403 verified). Client-approve endpoint intentionally inserts a submission_records row with status READY, and the case-read code correctly ignores non-SUBMITTED submission_records when computing has_submission_record and status_label — so approval alone never leaks 'Submitted to HMRC' into the UI.

Frontend MyTaxReturn.jsx correctly reads approvedVersion from cs.approved_version with a ?? calc?.version fallback, applies the 'with your accountant for submission to HMRC' wording, and only shows the recorded submission date when has_submission_record is true. Empty state 'Final documents will appear here once available.' verified.

Client isolation on final documents is enforced via the shared ownership gate (foreign client → 403/404 on download; id never appears in their list) — same guarantee proven in the 50-test isolation suite in earlier iterations.

One residual quality item (non-blocking): the two xdist parallel-worker races (see action items) should ideally be pinned by scoping their fixtures similarly to the way TestCrossRoleWorkflow and TestApprovalAndSubmissionModel are — pin sequential steps to one class so loadscope keeps them on a single worker.

success_rate.backend: 99.7% overall (336/337 unique tests; 100% on the 18 new My Tax Return tests). The 1 failure is a known xdist race that passes serially.
success_rate.frontend: 100% on /my-return desktop + mobile (all required strings present/absent as specified, no console errors of substance, final-docs-panel testid present).

test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md exactly. Mutating tests used disposable per-test QA clients (qa.mtr.<uuid>@qa-taxsimba.example.com) created via super-admin; demo clienta@/clientb@example.com used ONLY as read-only for the UI render check.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The four My Tax Return corrections (final documents empty-state + release+download+isolation, dynamic approved_version wording, submission model gated to admin record-submission not client-approve, and 2027 deadline derived from case tax year) are all working end-to-end. Do NOT change pytest.ini (-n 2 --dist loadscope). Run test_zz_demo_portal_state.py LAST if the suite ever creates cases on demo accounts (it did not this iteration — everything ran against disposable QA clients). The one intermittent failure (test_iteration7_audit::TestAccountantRBAC::test_accountant_cannot_see_other_accountant_case) passes in isolation and is a pre-existing xdist race, NOT related to these changes.
rca of the issue: The single flaky test failure under -n 2 --dist loadscope is caused by a second xdist worker creating additional cases/notifications while the audit-RBAC test iterates. Isolated pytest run passes deterministically. Mitigation: move the sequential steps into a single test class so loadscope keeps the entire flow on one worker, exactly as was already done for TestCrossRoleWorkflow and TestApprovalAndSubmissionModel.
